Companion Animal Travel Desk Procedures

This section helps the Companion Animal Travel Desk keep pet travel calm, safe, and fair for every customer.

Treat every animal case as a care-first matter, not a speed contest. Start with the traveler’s needs, the pet's condition, and the fit of the travel plan before you confirm anything. Give clear guidance in plain words, and make sure the traveler understands crate standards, feeding notes, check-in steps, and what to do if the journey changes. If a case needs review, move it through the stepwise chain rather than rushing to a guess, because careful handling protects the traveler and the animal.

When you receive a report about a delayed bag or crate, log the details right away and guide the traveler through the next steps with patience. <<FACT F118>> Keep the tone steady, avoid blame, and make sure the traveler knows which items were packed, where the crate was last seen, and what support will follow. If the issue involves an animal's comfort or health, bring in the proper reviewer at once and do not leave the traveler with a vague answer.

For minor injury concerns, document what happened, note the visible signs, and advise the traveler on the approved follow-up path. <<FACT F113>> Do not promise extra help that has not been approved, but do offer clear direction, a calm handoff, and a check on whether the pet is stable enough to continue. If a traveler is upset, listen first, then restate the next step in simple language so they can act without confusion.

Use this desk to protect the traveler's trust as much as the pet's welfare. Keep notes accurate, keep language respectful, and never push a case forward until the needed care checks are done. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty reviewer when you need support, and keep Aurelia Skyways informed through the proper channel.
